article: Field Guide to the kingdoms and peoples of the world From the mouth of the Nekhtou River to the southern shores of the continent of Shaugodone, the Solar Empire claims its land in the name of the immortal emperors that have watched over it as long as their history records. Part tropical paradise, part unforgiving desert, the homeland of the Dwarves is believed by many to be the birthplace of civilization as we know it. Those that inhabit the empire are called Sun Dwarves, distinct from Cold Dwarves, the product of an exodus that that split the empire some time in the ancient past. There, they build their massive monuments to their revered ancestors and sun deities, and practice a strange kind of necromancy that preserves their deceased emperors to watch over their lands even in death. Further north, we find realms inhabited by a mix of Cold Dwarves, Orcs and Ogres (See Orcs). Further still we find the unforgiving wastes of Kastrunn, inhabited only be snow beasts and bloodthirsty tribes of Jerren. Orcs are a race of sturdy, colorful creatures seemingly built to weather adversity. Standing on average nearly six and a half feet tall, they are not actually a naturally-occuring creature. In some ancient age of terror, they were created by some black magic to serve as peerless soldiers of darkness. Though freed from that yoke, their bred dedication to order and hierarchy persists. Industrious and organized, Orcish kingdoms tend to be militaristic affairs, and most orc kings are also greatest tactician in their land. Orcish military doctrine frowns on pre-emptive strikes, instead emphasizing extreme retributive action - "Crush your enemies hard enough that your children don't have to," as one famous tactician once said. Several Orc nations exist to the north of the Solar Empire, as well as in the lowlands of Seceth and the mountains of Flikx. Ogres, once thought to be a separate species from Orcs, instead seem to be grown from the same stock as the original orcs. Though they can interbreed, the idea is frowned on among most of both groups. They are welcome in the orcs' kingdoms and armies, however. When found in the wild, they tend to live in nomadic clans and tribes that shy away from contact with outsiders. Jerren are short, stocky creatures with pink skin, hairy feet and immense appetites. The thought of their warbands brings a chill to even the hardiest orcish commander. Known for their immense appetites, both for food, specifically meat, even more specifically still-living meat, and sexual perversion, they bring terror wherever they roam, turning on each other if they go too long without a raid. Little is known of their internal culture, for they are universally hostile towards other creatures. Elves are a curiosity among creatures of this world, in part because they are not truly of this world. Considered the youngest of the races of the world, the first elves were creatures of flesh created by entities of the writhing chaos outside of our world. Designed by these entities to be tall, fair, powerful, and universally alluring, their sorcerers and armies nearly brought about the ruin of the world. After their seeming extinction at the end of the last war, pockets came out of wherever they had been hiding and begged the other races for forgiveness, claiming to have broken their otherworldly masters' chains. Today, there is one elven city, a city in the clouds, built on the remains of the Eldritch Portal they originally came through. As they have become attuned to this world, the traces of otherworldly power are slowly fading. Those that retain it inhabit the upper echelons of their society, and though they would prefer it kept a secret, many of these aristocrats suffer from rages and manias comparable to the elves of old. There are believed to be two intelligent (if the Jerren can be said to be intelligent) species currently inhabiting this world that evolved through normal means. However, if recent paleological and archaeological findings on the barely-explored continent of Vutis are to be believed, there once lived a third race, a race of tall dwarfoids, more slight than a dwarf or orc, yet not so tall or lithe as an elf. Judging by the ruins left behind, they possessed an understanding of technology on par with the more advanced orc nations, and a complex language which is just now being deciphered. It is truly and exciting time to be alive, dear reader, that such wonders have yet to be uncovered.

article: Legged robots traversing in confined environments could find their only path is blocked by obstacles. In circumstances where the obstacles are movable, a multilegged robot can manipulate the obstacles using its appendages to clear a path and continue with its mission. This strategy is referred to as obstacle manipulation, which involves using the robot's limbs to apply forces or torques to the obstacles in order to move them out of the way. Obstacle manipulation can be particularly useful for addressing challenging terrain, such as rubble or other debris, as well as situations where confined spaces make it difficult to maneuver. For example, a robot exploring a cave system may encounter large boulders blocking its path. Instead of attempting to climb over or around the boulders, the robot could use its limbs to push the rocks out of the way and continue forward. To accomplish obstacle manipulation, multilegged robots typically require specialized end-effectors, such as grippers or claws, to grasp and manipulate objects. Additionally, advanced control algorithms and sensing systems are necessary to enable the robot to detect and respond to changes in the environment, as well as monitor the force and torque being applied to the obstacles.

article: Sunlight contains ultraviolet light which can break down some molecules. This includes breaking down pigment molecules in your hair, which leaves you with lighter hair. In your cells this can mean breaking down your DNA, which is bad news bears. To combat this your body produces another compound - melanin - which absorbs ultraviolet light, and surrounds the nucleus of your cells (where the DNA is stored) with it. Melanin causes the dark color. So really what it comes down to is that your skin is still alive and able to try to protect itself from future damage, while your hair is dead and subject to the damage it takes.

article: This work presents dense stereo reconstruction using high-resolution images for infrastructure inspections. The state-of-the-art stereo reconstruction methods, both learning and non-learning ones, consume too much computational resource on high-resolution data. Recent learning-based methods achieve top ranks on most benchmarks. However, they suffer from the generalization issue due to lack of task-specific training data. We propose to use a less resource demanding non-learning method, guided by a learning-based model, to handle high-resolution images and achieve accurate stereo reconstruction. The deep-learning model produces an initial disparity prediction with uncertainty for each pixel of the down-sampled stereo image pair. The uncertainty serves as a self-measurement of its generalization ability and the per-pixel searching range around the initially predicted disparity. The downstream process performs a modified version of the Semi-Global Block Matching method with the up-sampled per-pixel searching range. The proposed deep-learning assisted method is evaluated on the Middlebury dataset and high-resolution stereo images collected by our customized binocular stereo camera. The combination of learning and non-learning methods achieves better performance on 12 out of 15 cases of the Middlebury dataset. In our infrastructure inspection experiments, the average 3D reconstruction error is less than 0.004m.

It's a tradition in our family. And now A coughing fit racked Earl's frail form. Connor watched, wishing he could help. "Now, I'd like to show it to you. Keep it for your grandson, but I don't want you to forget about it. I'd like you to keep this in your wallet for those gloomy days." "I don't have a wallet." "You don't? Well, then, we'll have to fix that." Earl emptied the contents of his wallet onto the bed next to him. He held out the wallet to Connor who took it reverently. "Promise me you won't forget, Connor." "I won't forget. I promise." Tears spilled freely down Connor's face. "Look in the billfold pocket." Grandpa Earl smiled in contentment and closed his eyes. Connor opened the wallet, the softened leather creaking but inaudible over the sound of the machines surrounding his grandfather. article: All aeroplanes are steered with control surfaces. "Ailerons" on the outer edges of the wings move up and down to cause the aeroplane to roll left and right. "Elevators" on the horizontal tailplane move up and down to cause the nose of the aircraft to point up or down. And the "rudder" on the vertical tailplane moves left and right, to cause the nose of the aircraft to point left or right. In a simple aircraft, these control surfaces are moved by being directly connected to the pilots' controls by cables and pulleys. In most airliners, the controls are too heavy to be moved by cables. Instead, the pilots' controls directly command a hydraulic system to move the control surfaces. If the pilot pulls back on the controls, the hydraulics immediately cause the elevators to move, so the aircraft's nose points up. In fly-by-wire systems, the controls do not directly affect the hydraulics. Instead, the position of the controls is fed to a computer. The computer processes this information, possibly combining it with other information. It is then the computer which instructs the hydraulics to move the flying surfaces. There are lots of advantages of this. In Airbus aircraft, it allows the computer to be put into different modes for different phases of flight, adjusting how the controls respond to pilot inputs. It allows the computer to override the pilot in certain circumstances. It also allows the computer to process the input from the two pilots separately (although it's quite debatable whether this is an advantage or a disadvantage). In the Eurofighter Typhoon, fly-by-wire is essential. The aircraft design is inherently unstable. This allows it to outmanoeuvre pretty much any other aircraft - but it means that the control inputs which have to be made just to keep it flying in a straight line are too difficult for a human pilot to be able to do. The pilot instructs the computer, using normal flying controls, and the computer works out what needs to be done to not only comply with the pilot's requests, but also to overcome the instability of the aircraft, and it combines these two things together and moves the control surfaces accordingly.

article: In recent years, sequence-to-sequence models have been very effective for end-to-end grammatical error correction (GEC). As creating human-annotated parallel corpus for GEC is expensive and time-consuming, there has been work done on unsupervised GEC approaches that do not require parallel corpora. One such approach is using self-supervised learning, where the model learns to predict whether an input sentence is grammatically correct or not by comparing it to a slightly modified version of itself. This way, the model can learn to identify and correct grammatical errors without relying on any labeled data. Another approach is to use contextual embeddings such as BERT or ELMO to identify erroneous words or phrases in a sentence based on their context. These embeddings are pre-trained on large amounts of text data and can capture the meaning and context of words in a sentence. This approach also does not require any labeled data and can help in identifying and correcting grammatical errors in a sentence. There is also work done on using neural machine translation (NMT) models for GEC, where the model is trained on parallel corpora of correct and incorrect sentences in different languages, and it learns to translate the incorrect sentences to their corresponding correct versions. This approach requires labeled parallel corpora, but the advantage is that it can handle more complex grammatical errors that are difficult to identify using rule-based or statistical approaches. Overall, there is ongoing research in developing unsupervised and semi-supervised approaches for GEC, which can reduce the reliance on human-annotated parallel corpora and make the GEC process more scalable and cost-effective.

The goal is to optimize the encoding and decoding strategies to minimize the distortion at the decoders subject to a total power constraint at the encoders. Several techniques have been proposed to solve this problem, including joint source-channel coding, distributed source-channel coding, and layered transmission. The choice of technique depends on the specifics of the application and the desired trade-offs between complexity, delay, and performance. Overall, the design of transmission strategies for correlated sources over multiple access relay channels with time asynchronism is an active research area with many practical applications, including wireless sensor networks, mobile communications, and social media.

article: Sgt. Surge awoke to a bright light. He got up briefly before the weight of his head pulled him back to the pillow with a light thump. "I guess I made it..." he mumbled to himself. He looked around for the familiar yellow lump, but he didn't see him anywhere. "Pikachu..." he mumbled. Lifting his head, he sees the bed right across from him, laying there, now Raichu. "I guess I had to..." Months ago, his unit was assigned to holding a beach. He rose the ranks quickly, but, you need an evolved Pokemon to become an officer. Though he could have passed the officer candidates training with flying colors, he never wanted to evolve the Pikachu he had as a boy. Friends since childhood after all. He figured, Pikachu was happy being who he is, there's no reason to change him just for an extra pip on his collar. But that changed 5 days ago. It was a quiet day like any other. Blue skies, a nice sea breeze. He and his unit was thinking about having a bbq later in the day. Guard duty is always quiet. But suddenly, they all heard a large thump; a large pokeball fell onto their beach. Puzzled, Bobby and his squirtle went to inspect it, but before anyone realized what happened, it rolled around, glowed, and self destructed. Suddenly, overhead, large shadows of Farrows and Pidgeot loomed overhead, dropping more voltorbs onto our position. Half the unit was wiped out as the voltorbs kept self destructing all over the place. Sgt. Surge barely had time to run to his fox hole with Pikachu before a Voltorb narrowly missed his head. As soon as it began, it stopped. They all peered over the edges of their fox holes, and to their horror, an entire aquatic commando team was inbound. As far as they can tell, commandos riding their Blastoise, Starmie, and Cloisters dotted the horizon. He ordered his platoon to begin firing. Pikachu sent bolts of lightning all over the horizon. His buddy Tim began loading his Graveler up with rocks to throw. Tom was out there with his Diglet re-digging every trench to slow down the advance, but it was no use. One by one, he watched his unit members fall has cannons of water and ice began covering their beach. Sarge was desperate, he had to do something. And so he reached into his pocketed, and pulled out the lightning stone. He looked at Pikachu, he looked back with sadness in his eyes. As Sarge reached out his right hand to touch the stone to Pikachu. Pikachu bowed his head, and acknowledged this was the only way, and one last time, said "pika.." A bright light enveloped Pikachu as he evolved. Quickly, he ordered the now Raichu to unleash all the thunder and lightning and thunderbolts he can. And that's all he remembers as they both passed out from exertion. Waking up in the hospital together, at least they made it out alive. Suddenly, the door opened and Captain Lance walked in. "Surge!" he said. "You did well today, if it weren't for your Raichu wiping out the water and air invasion, we would have lost the beachhead for sure. Not to mention the remainder of your platoon!." "And the rest of my men and their Pokemon sir?" Surge muttered in reply. "It seems, unfortunately, over half your unit was wiped out including your Lieutenant. But fear not, we have a new batch of recruits to reform your platoon. You will all be going back to the front once you all recover in the next week. The 75th Pokemon armored needs gamma platoon and, gamma platoon needs a leader. With your new Raichu, I think you would be an excellent choice for an officer. So, congratulations, Lt. Surge. You did well today." Capt. Lance saluted, turned away abruptly and walked out. Surge couldn't think or process what just happened, it's all still a blur. With half his friends gone and now in charge, it seemed overwhelming. But none of this would be impossible to handle if only he still had his Pikachu. If only he didn't lose his bestfriend, nay, transform his best friend into a war machine..... maybe he could have handled all his burdens. And maybe, his right hand would stop shaking.

article: "This is never going to sell." Thomas Jefferson Carter, owner and lead editor at Herald Publishing, set his half-sipped gin and tonic on the desk and shoved the manuscript towards me as if the words themselves stunk. Literally. The grandfather clock ticked dutifully. I waited twelve ticks before speaking. "Why not?" "Some of this technology..... it seems far-fetched. Touching pieces of glasses and having images and words come up on them..... books read from some sort of electric library, telegraphs appearing in the palm of your hand, being able not only to speak to but SEE another man from anywhere in the world..." "How is it more far-fetched than Wells or Verne? Than time travel or journeying to the center of the earth?" Carter mumbled to himself, his lips squashing his knee-jerk replies into mush while he chose his answer. "In your story, it seems as if humanity is more connected than ever before, and yet they waste it." " 'T is the definition of'dystopia', sir." Carter's eyes hardened. Once more my wit had outrun my wisdom. "Your story proclaims that we will use all of this achievement for nothing but self-gratifcation. We will use these instant telegraphs to argue with each other over the latest showtunes or the proper length of a woman's skirt. We will not use these portable..... what did you call them?" "Tablets." "We will not use these tablets like Moses did, to carry down the inspiration of God or show a divine truth. We won't even use them to show the greatest wonders of the world to every curious child. In your story, we use them to print pictures of ourselves, to challenge each other to tedious bouts of bantering or to pointless little competitions. It's as if..... these people have no real problems." "Why would there be, sir? You've read the papers, seen the newsreels. They're calling it "the War to end all Wars" over there in Europe. After they're done shelling each other into paste, humanity's taste for blood might finally be sated. Then what will we argue about? Once we see mankind for what it is, one people with the same hopes and dreams and fears, then what is left to divide us?" Carter's chair squeaked as he leaned forward. "So you're saying we make our own problems because all the true problems have been solved?" "I am." The grandfather clock ticked thirteen times. "It's as if your story is a utopian one wrapped up in dystopia. Humanity's greatest achievements will bring about it's greatest boredom." "I like to see myself as a optimistic cynic, sir." He took another sip of his drink and considered the manuscript again. He touched the edge of it, testing to see if, as a result of our conversation, the pages had turned to gold. "No, it'll still never sell. Try again."

article: We consider a multi-agent resource allocation setting that models the assignment of papers to reviewers. A recurring issue in allocation problems is the compatibility of welfareefficiency and fairness. Given an oracle to find a welfare-achieving allocation, we embed such an oracle into a flexible algorithm called the Constrained Round Robin (CRR) algorithm, that achieves the required welfare level. Our algorithm also allows the system designer to lower the welfare requirements in order to achieve a higher degree of fairness. If the welfare requirement is lowered enough, a strengthening of envy-freeness up to one item is guaranteed. Hence, our algorithm can be viewed as a computationally efficient way to interpolate between welfare and approximate envy-freeness in allocation problems.

article: I am surprised nobody has given you a correct answer yet. Forgive me for not pretending you are five. Let's say you are a billionaire. You have a billion dollars. You don't keep it all in cash under your mattress. In fact, you don't keep it in a savings account at a bank, either, at least not very much of it. Most of your billion dollars is actually something you own which is worth a billion dollars. Property, stock, mutual funds, etc. The way taxes work in the US, you don't pay taxes on what you own. You pay taxes on your income. That income could be from salary, or from a profitable investment. But investments are special, because there is no income until you sell them for more money than you initially paid for them. So let's say you own a billion dollars worth of mutual funds. Over the course of the year, it grows 8 in value. That is an 80 million dollar increase in value. But unless you sell some of it, there is no income, so there is no tax. You are 80 million dollars richer, but you have paid no taxes. Now, hang on a second. You do need some money to live on. Let's say a million dollars this year - that should be enough. So you sell a million dollars worth of this mutual fund you own. You will have to pay taxes on this. But not on a million dollars, just on the difference between what you paid for it and what you sold it for. Let's say the difference is 20 since you initially bought it a few years ago. You will pay taxes on 200k. Also, because this is a special kind of income called capital gains, you will pay a lower tax rate than if it were your salary. Instead of 30 or more, you will pay 20. 40k. So, you are 80 million dollars richer this year. Your tax bill is 40 thousand dollars. Your effective tax rate was one twentieth of one percent. 0.05 Not 5, not 0.5. 0.05. Edit: Fixed my math.,Billionaires make most of their money off various sorts of investment income (which affects a very small percentage of the population) rather than payroll taxes (which affect most people). Given the total tax liability of a typical billionaire, it's usually very cost-effective to do some combination of restructuring their income to avoid taxes (relatively easy, since they're probably a CEO or major shareholder of a company that employs lots of high-level accountants), or lobby the relevant national government to add a few tax loopholes that benefit billionaires with their specific income structure. In other words, you don't need to understand the details of the "variable prepaid forward contract;" the important thing to understand is that once you make a sufficiently insane amount of money, it's much cheaper to game the tax system than to pay your fair share.','Adding to what Wurm42 said, billionaires can afford structured tax shelters, overseas corporations, and the really big fish can pay major law firms for "legal opinion" letters that are then indemnified by the law firm if the billionaire gets sued by the IRS. In other words, the billionaire gets a letter from a lawyer telling him some tax dodge is legal. If the IRS challenges the deduction, then the billionaire can claim he was innocently following the advice of council while the law firm defends him.', "A much more concrete example is that most wealthy people make much of their money from investment vehicles, which include the selling of stock or property. When an asset is sold for more than one bought it for, it's called a capital gain. As such, when one makes money from capital gains, it isn't taxed at a regular income tax level like the money you earn from a job. Rather, it's taxed a lower rate. Currently, long-term capital gains (assets held for more than a year) are taxed at a flat 15 for most income tax brackets. And the kicker here is that if your income is actually in the lowest two brackets of 10 and 15, you aren't taxed on those long-term capital gains. I imagine that most of the wealthiest people have a low reported income because they aren't working a typical job, so they fall into the lowest tax bracket. Most of their income that dictates their brackets would be from dividends from stocks or property income.,I don't know the answer to how the specific tactic you describe works, but in general... Tax rates are based on taxable income. This is different from the actual amount of income you have, because tax law allows people to exclude certain types of income from 'counting' as taxable. For example, if you pay interest on your home loan, you get to say "that money doesn't count as income" to the IRS, and so you don't have to pay tax on that part. If you contribute income to a 401k, you don't have to count that either. And, certain ways of getting income (like the sale of your home) don't count as taxable income. Very wealthy people don't get as much of their income through obvious sources like a paycheck, and because they have large volumes of money they have opportunities to shelter more of their income which is a way of saying that they can do things with their income that make it "not count" as taxable. article: (So I worked out a concept based on the idea, taking it into a little more extreme direction. I found the concept really interesting, especially taking it to its logical conclusions of brain enhancement. I may have took the'Religion' part a little too literally, but if you're interested in more or more detail about the world I was thinking of, let me know.) Even for the trusted, it's a hassle getting down here. Three biometric scanners get me into the Ecclasiarchy's data center. Bodyscan, DNA, mental key. I stand in the final chamber, listening to the low-volume hymns in soft white light, and think of the well-worn pages of the bible on the lectern, the first day I gave a sermon. The light flicks on, a golden-white, and the door hisses and opens. It's pointless really, the thing could have verified who I was without me having to do anything, but we've always held ourselves to tradition. The hum of cooling systems is all I can hear; the man-sized blocks of alabaster computing substrate aren't hot enough to glow on their own, but they do radiate heat if you get close enough. I'm tech support now, well, I'm still a priest. But there's an ever-increasing personnel shortage and we all end up doing double duty somewhere. The facility's Seraphim dispatched little more than a shade of a angel saying some piece of equipment down here needed maintenance, so I'm here, in my robes, and a toolbox. I know if the Seraphim wasn't able to fix it remotely it's going to be a pain in the posterior. Walking past those alabaster pillars you can't help but think about what they represent. One hundred forty five million and counting. Looking directly at one, I could almost hear a choir of angels in my head. My metabrain said it was a synesthetic thing, that I was doing it to myself, but I wouldn't put it past the Seraphim to add a little trickery to it all. They're all devious bastards in some ways, God forgive me. My own modest neural circuitry pointed me in the right direction, down hundreds of rows of radiant white substrate like gigantic tombstones laid out in a perfect grid. Rounding the final corner, the ground was covered in hundreds of coppery, metal swirls, spread out like someone dropped a jar of them. Copper shavings. Looking at the scatter, they all seemed to have come from what looked like a dead camera. What could have happened here? The camera dome had a blackened hole where the ultrahard material had fractured outward. Some kind of overload? I unfolded a step ladder, and took the panel off the ceiling with a crowbar, reaching up to the conduit. These things are quadruply redundant, built to last out of nanospecced material, internal power supply, wireless, conduit backed up. I grabbed my headlamp and looked around in the ceiling space. The conduit was severed, pinched on two ends with something strong enough to bend the metal until the interior links were cut. More copper shavings everywhere. The area around the camera had been sawn open, cleanly. I shook my head. It looked like sabotage, but how? And what use was sabotaging one camera? Exiting the ceiling I looked from the hole in the camera's dome forward. On the substrate pillar around 4 meters away, there was a black dot. I rushed over to it, triggering a gentle haptic feedback from my brain as I approached the personnel restricted boundary and could go no closer. But from there I could see the black dot; A little spike embedded in the substrate. Invaders in heaven. I instantly called for help, and found my sensorium elevated through the choirs almost instantly to the Seraphim's level. Couldn't even look at the thing directly of course, but it didn't waste time asking any questions, just rifled through my brain for the appropriate information. I'm guessing. In the church you sign away your own private key for that stuff to the Administration. A matter of trust. An insane thing to do anywhere else in the world, but if I didn't buy into the whole righteous-servants-of-God-on-earth thing I wouldn't even be here. Of course men are fallible, even the most righteous man is, but the Angels are not. If they fail in anything, it was because it was impossible, not because it was an oversight. And it solved the problem of those lip-service priests with ulterior motives, no force on Earth could lie so thoroughly to itself that these things couldn't see their true colors. My sensorium returned to the real world as quickly as it was snatched away, my body steadfastly holding itself up until I resumed control. There were no lights on the attacked substrate in front of me, but I could tell something had been done. It just didn't seem to glow the same.

article: Let v c (G), f v s (G) and o c t (G), respectively, denote the size of a minimum vertex cover, minimum feedback vertex set and minimum odd cycle transversal in a graph G . One can ask, when looking for these sets in a graph, how much bigger might they be if we require that they are independent; that is, what is the price of independence ? If G has a vertex cover, feedback vertex set or odd cycle transversal that is an independent set, then we let i v c (G), i f v s (G) or i o c t (G), respectively, denote the minimum size of such a set. Similar to a recent study on the price of connectivity (Hartinger et al. EuJC 2016), we investigate for which graphs H the values of i v c (G), i f v s (G) and i o c t (G) are bounded in terms of v c (G), f v s (G) and o c t (G), respectively, when the graph G belongs to the class of H -free graphs. We find complete classifications for vertex cover and feedback vertex set and an almost complete classification for odd cycle transversal (subject to three non-equivalent open cases). We also investigate for which graphs H the values of i v c (G), i f v s (G) and i o c t (G) are equal to v c (G), f v s (G) and o c t (G), respectively, when the graph G belongs to the class of H -free graphs. We find a complete classification for vertex cover and almost complete classifications for feedback vertex set (subject to one open case) and odd cycle transversal (subject to three open cases).

article: Automatic annotation of temporal expressions is a research challenge of great interest in the field of information extraction. In this report, I describe a novel rule-based architecture, built on top of existing natural language processing tools, to automatically annotate temporal expressions in text data. The architecture consists of several modules, each responsible for a specific task in the annotation process. The first module is a pre-processing module that applies several text normalization techniques to standardize different textual representations of the same temporal expression. This normalization promotes consistency in the annotation process. The second module is a pattern matching module, where a set of regular expressions is defined to identify temporal expressions of interest in the text. article: The rain from the thunderstorm outside lashed against the train as I strode down the aisle, dripping from the deluge outside. There'd been delays all morning, and this train was unusually crowded as a result. Every seat seemed to be occupied, the cars packed with humans in various states of bedragglement. I had just about given up hope, resigning myself to standing, when I noticed an empty seat at the end of the car. Gratefully, I made my way over and plonked myself down next to a brown-haired girl who couldn't have been more than ten. She looked up at me as I sat down and gave a faint but warm smile. I couldn't help returning it, thankful to finally have found a spot to take the weight off my feet. As I did, I noticed the girl's hands, resting gently on her legs. Each hand was loosely holding a cell phone. They were the same model, as far as I could tell, though I wasn't sure exactly which model it was. They looked older, like something from the early 2000s. The one in her left hand was black, while the one in her right hand was white. She followed my gaze, angling her head downward to peer at her own hands. She blinked. Then, she lifted her head again, looking right into my eyes. Now she was positively beaming. I was taken slightly aback, but I was still feeling quite pleased to have found a seat at all, and the girl's smile was infectious. I grinned back in spite of myself. "What's got you so chuffed?" I asked, in good humor. The girl continued to smile, but shook her head slightly. I looked at her for a moment, and then it was my turn to blink. The girl was still looking at me, and still grinning like a Cheshire cat. I cleared my throat, as my smile became more fixed. With a jerk that I had vainly hoped would look natural, I moved my head and began making a show of looking for the morning's paper, which I'd stashed in my briefcase. When I'd retrieved it, the girl was placidly staring out the window, watching as the water rushed down the pane in rivulets. Her hands remained in her lap, loosely holding the phones. Confused, but also somewhat relieved, I turned to the financial section to finish an article on precious metals that I'd been perusing early. When I finished, I leafed to the crossword puzzle, using the cover of turning pages to steal a glance at my tiny seatmate. She had not moved, and I found myself smiling slightly, as I wondered about this unusual child and her two cell phones. Presently, I turned my attention back to my paper and busied myself decoding a few clues. It was just a few minutes later that the train began to slow, heralding our imminent arrival. I folded my paper, reaching down for my briefcase, as the train slowed to a stop. I felt something brush against my leg and caught the flash of a brown ponytail as it weaved into the crowd, disappearing amongst my fellow commuters. Chuckling slightly, I lifted my briefcase and made to stand when something caught my eye - the girl's cellphone, the black one. I pursed my lips - I didn't really have time for this - and reached out towards the phone. It immediately started to ring, moving slightly across the seat as it vibrated. I withdrew my hand. The ringing stopped. The furrow in my brow increased and, telling myself I was being silly, I reached out again for the old phone. Again it started to ring. I hesitated. The phone was almost off the seat now, the vibration moving it steadily closer to the edge. I scooped it up and looked at it. The screen was illuminated but there was nothing to read, just an artificial blue-white glow. The ringing continued. Almost without meaning to, I pushed the green call button, and put the phone to my ear. "Hallo?" Static. A musical, tinkling laugh. Then nothing. The screen had gone dark. I held the phone in my hand, frowning down at it. Shrugging, I slipped it into my pocket and exited the train, hastening to catch the last of the stragglers moving into the station. So focused was I on my destination that I didn't see the small girl in front of me, and almost bowled her over. I skidded to a stop on the rain soaked concrete, just inches from the girl. "You gave me quite a fright," I said, half relieved, half annoyed. The girl merely smiled at me, making no move to apologize or step to the side. I blinked. Again. Coming back to myself, I plunged my hand into the pocket of my coat, drawing out the black phone. I held it out to the girl, who continued smiling impassively. "You forgot this," I said, somewhat (in my opinion) gratuitously. But the girl only smiled wider, staring into my eyes as she ignored the phone in front of her. Slowly, she shook her head. "Keep it." Her voice was deeper and richer than it should have been, aged and full-bodied. It was the voice of a woman, not the small girl standing beside me. Inadvertently, I took a step back. The girl's eyes seemed to sparkle with mischief, as her smile stretched to its largest size yet, relegating her eyes to twin twinkling slits. "Keep it," she repeated. And with a swish of her ponytail, she was gone, melting back into the crowd of the station. I stood rooted to the spot, staring at the black phone still clutched in my hand. It was warm, with a reassuring weight, and almost without thinking, I went to pocket it. I had just felt the tiny bounce as the phone came to a rest against my thigh, breaking my reverie, when I heard the barest hint of a voice float over the assembled crowd: "And next time, pick up on the first call."
label: human

article: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have demonstrated dominating performance in many fields; since AlexNet, networks used in practice are going wider and deeper. We only make two assumptions: the inputs are non-degenerate and the network is over-parameterized. The latter means the network width is sufficiently large: polynomial in L , the number of layers and in n , the number of samples. Our key technique is to derive that, in a sufficiently large neighborhood of the random initialization, the optimization landscape is almost-convex and semi-smooth even with ReLU activations. This implies an equivalence between over-parameterized neural networks and neural tangent kernel (NTK) in the finite (and polynomial) width setting. As concrete examples, starting from randomly initialized weights, we prove that SGD can attain 100 training accuracy in classification tasks, or minimize regression loss in linear convergence speed, with running time polynomial in n , L . Our theory applies to the widely-used but non-smooth ReLU activation, and to any smooth and possibly non-convex loss functions. article: When you clap, you send out sound waves. When two sound waves meet each other, they'interfere'. Imagine waves on water when you drop a stone into it. When two waves are in phase (their peaks and troughs line up), they will enhance each other and create a louder sound. This is called constructive interference. On the other hand, when two waves are out of phase (their peaks and troughs are opposite), they will cancel each other out and create silence. This is called destructive interference. Understanding sound wave interference is important in many fields, including music, acoustics, and telecommunications. It can also be useful in noise reduction and noise cancellation technologies.

article: [."com domains are administrated by Verisign. A few companies have arrangements with Verisign to sell domains. For the most part, these companies don't actually sell domains to customers, but to the next level of registrars. This third (or fourth, if you count ICANN) level is where most people actually buy domains..uk is similar, but administrated by Nominet.,ICANN, the entity that assigns addresses and domain names and stuff, began life as a US company, and still is, though less directly and more complicatedly than it was. The problem, that's been the subject of all those UN meetings recently, and lots of other meetings since there even was an internet, is that for technical reasons, it's so impractical for anybody to "control" the internet without biting off their nose to spite their face. You may have seen people complain from time to time that someone is "stealing" their website code, and what can they do to keep people from doing that. Some nerd will explain to them that their code can't be made really impossible to get - and still be seen in a browser, because of the way browsers work. They can make it harder, so that only nerdier people will be able to get it, but they can't make it impossible. The only way you can be sure I can't steal your images is to keep them on your desktop - don't put them on the internet! Which, of course, means nobody can see them, either. That's kind of how it is with the internet itself. The only way they can really control it is to turn it off completely, and disable all the stuff that makes wireless access work as well, everywhere. That would mean companies couldn't make money from it, regimes couldn't use it to promote their policies, or to monitor what people are saying about them. Because it's been in such common use for over 20 years now, turning it off would create a huge mess, because so much business is done on the internet, from individuals paying their utility bills to rich men making huge deals to make more money. This is one of the things that makes the internet unique in our human history: the US, or the UN, or whoever, can claim to own the internet, they can be officially in charge of handing out the numbers that go with domain names. But the people all over the world who use the internet are the ones who decide what's on it. Sure, a regime or an internet service provider can "take down" a website. But when they do, 9000 people put up copies of it. If they try to take down those 9000, for each one, another 9000 copies go up. And the people who put up the copies are better nerds than the regime, so it keeps getting harder and harder, and more expensive, to find out where the damn things really are to take them down! And by now, the internet has layers! There's the "deep web," all that stuff you read about onion and Tor, where traffic is routed and rerouted and encrypted so hard that - well, somebody smart will have to come explain if it would even be technically possible to "find" somebody. tldr: lots of entities would like to, but you can't put toothpaste back in the tube. Either they shut it down, and nobody makes money, or they leave it up - and put up with us! article: This paper proposes a robust adversarial reinforcement learning (RARL) -based multi-access point (AP) coordination method that is robust even against unexpected decentralized operations of uncoordinated APs. Multi-AP coordination is a challenging task, as it requires multiple APs to work together to optimize network performance while avoiding interference and congestion. Adversarial reinforcement learning is a machine learning approach that involves training agents to make decisions in a competitive environment, where each agent is trying to maximize its own reward while also trying to interfere with the other agents' performance. The proposed RARL-based method uses a centralized controller to coordinate the actions of multiple APs in a way that maximizes network throughput while minimizing interference. The controller uses a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to optimize the coordination policy, taking into account the dynamic nature of the network and the presence of competing agents. The RARL approach is particularly useful in situations where there is a high degree of uncertainty, as it allows the controller to adapt its policies in real-time based on the actions of the other APs. This makes the system more robust and resilient to unexpected events, such as malfunctions or unplanned changes in the network topology. Overall, the proposed RARL-based multi-AP coordination method has the potential to significantly improve the performance and reliability of wireless networks, particularly in environments with multiple competing APs.

article: A shortcoming of existing reachability approaches for nonlinear systems is the poor scalability with the number of continuous state variables. To mitigate this problem we present a simulation-based approach where we use a combination of Monte Carlo simulation and machine learning techniques to approximate the reach set of the nonlinear system. By generating a large number of random initial states and simulating the system's trajectories, we obtain a representative sample of the system's behavior. Then, by training a machine learning model on this sample data, we can approximate the reach set for the system much more efficiently compared to traditional methods. This approach has several advantages over existing methods. Firstly, it can handle systems with a large number of continuous state variables without suffering from poor scalability. Secondly, it does not require the computation of the system's exact dynamics or the solution of complex optimization problems. Finally, it allows for quick exploration of the system's behavior and can be used to analyze the impact of various inputs on the system's reachability. Overall, simulation-based reachability analysis can help us quickly understand the behavior of nonlinear systems and support decision-making in various applications, such as robotics, control systems, and autonomous vehicles.

article: Deep video recognition is more computationally expensive than image recognition, especially on large-scale datasets like Kinetics. Therefore, training scalability is essential to handle a large amount of videos. In this context, distributed training methods are often used, which allow for training on multiple machines in parallel. One approach to distributed training is data parallelism, where a copy of the model is trained on each worker with a subset of the data. The gradients from each worker are then averaged and used to update the global model parameters. This method can be efficient for models with large numbers of parameters, but can be limited by the communication overhead between workers. Another approach is model parallelism, where different segments of the model are trained on different workers. This method can be more efficient for models with large numbers of layers, but can be limited by the memory constraints of each worker. Finally, hybrid approaches can be used, which combine both data and model parallelism to take advantage of the benefits of both approaches. Overall, distributed training methods are essential for training deep video recognition models on large-scale datasets, as they allow for improved scalability and reduced training time.

I felt that if I saw one little bit of information, one tiny thing, I would figure out what was happening. Or, more importantly, who I was. It was by this point I realised that I was stark naked, and quickly grabbed a towel hanging off a table on the right side of the room to save my embarrassment. After I wrapped the towel around my waist, I paused for thought. ' Why would I be embarrassed? There's no one here.' But, certainly, there was someone here earlier. A cup of coffee, still steaming, sat on the table. A Computer on the opposite side of the room was switched on, prominently displaying a document containing a wall of text. I decided to investigate further. Sitting at the computer, I scrolled through the text, which seemed like a sort of speech that one would present to an audience, and, through the eloquent wordings and descriptions, I figured out two things. One, this room belonged to a scientist. Two, they were on the verge of a breakthrough. This breakthrough in particular interested me, partly due to my curiosity, but mostly due to the way they described it as " The most astonishing breakthrough in scientific history. After taking my good look at the machine, I turned to the table, picking up a note with copious amounts of equations, underlinings and encircled passages scattered across the page. The second pod was still closed. Jogging towards it, I smiled, gripping the handle, and pulling open the door, readying myself to greet whomever was inside. Dead, empty sockets. Grey, peeling skin. article: Ensemble models comprising of deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) have shown significant improvements in model generalization but at the cost of large computation and memory requirements. Our framework provides two main benefits: i) Distilling knowledge from different teachers into the student network promotes heterogeneity in learning features at different branches of the student network and enables the network to learn diverse solutions to the target problem. ii) Coupling the branches of the student network through ensembling encourages collaboration and improves the quality of the final predictions by reducing variance in the network outputs. Experiments on the well established CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets show that our Ensemble Knowledge Distillation (EKD) improves classification accuracy and model generalization especially in situations with limited training data. article: We study the problem of selecting the best sampling set for bandlimited reconstruction of signals on graphs. A frequency domain representation for graph signals can be defined using the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of variation operators that take into account the underlying graph connectivity. Smoothly varying signals defined on the nodes are of particular interest in various applications, and tend to be approximately bandlimited in the frequency basis. Sampling theory for graph signals deals with the problem of choosing the best subset of nodes for reconstructing a bandlimited signal from its samples. Most approaches to this problem require a computation of the frequency basis (i.e., the eigenvectors of the variation operator), followed by a search procedure using the basis elements. This can be impractical, in terms of storage and time complexity, for real datasets involving very large graphs. We circumvent this issue in our formulation by introducing quantities called graph spectral proxies , defined using the powers of the variation operator, in order to approximate the spectral content of graph signals. This allows us to formulate a direct sampling set selection approach that does not require the computation and storage of the basis elements. We show that our approach also provides stable reconstruction when the samples are noisy or when the original signal is only approximately bandlimited. Furthermore, the proposed approach is valid for any choice of the variation operator, thereby covering a wide range of graphs and applications. We demonstrate its effectiveness through various numerical experiments.

article: Pharmacist here. First of all, caffeine has a few different ways that it works so that complicates all the following explanations even further. This is the case for MANY drugs and has to do with genetics and tolerance due to enzyme induction. (Okay, left the ELI5 track for a second.) There is a fairly new speciality in pharmacy (yes, there are pharmacists who specialize) called pharmacogenomics which studies these differences with the hope of better matching patients to drugs. (Blood pressure meds can have wildly different effects from patient to patient. That's why there are still so many different ones on the market.) Someday, we'll be able to use a person's genome to help physicians prescribe the proper drug rather than use the hit-and-miss method used now. Also, drugs can be designed for certain genotypes. (People with a certain gene or set of genes.) Resistance to certain drugs or unexpected effects from certain drugs are usually inherited. But even within a certain family, people maybe affected differently by the same drug at the same concentration. Also, people can become more tolerant to a drug if they are exposed to it a lot over time. This involves the liver and kidneys, which are the two major ways a drug is removed from the blood and therefore from the body. So, yes, people have different brain chemistry but some of the answers on here make it sound as though we're all wildly different in brain chemistry and that's just not true. There are subtle differences and some of them are physical rather than chemical. A drug must cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB) to get into the nervous system. This barrier is a defense and the more "oily" a drug is, the easier it is for it to cross. (nonpolar vs. polar) A small difference in the effectiveness of the BBB can make a big difference in how much of a certain drug gets through. Also, the permeability of different parts of the brain to certain drugs can make a difference in which parts of the brain are most affected by a drug. Is it the reticular formation, which plays a big role in wakefulness? Is it the hippocampus, which is the major brain structure dealing with memory? Etc. And everyone is also right in that all of these things can change as we age. It seems nothing in the body undergoes more changes from birth to elderly death than the central nervous system. Every time we learn something new it changes a tiny part of our brain and who knows what kind of longterm or "butterfly" effect this change could cause? Damn, I love neurology!

article: I didn't know. I swear I didn't know. If I had known the price, I never would have stopped time. I would have just forgotten about it, and moved on with my life. But I was selfish. The first time it happened was in a parking lot the night after Christmas. I was putting away groceries, when out of nowhere, a truck swerved around the corner and came barreling right towards me. I could have rolled out of the way, but instead I stood there, dumbfounded. This guy must have been drunk and decided to joyride through the parking lot. In that moment, I knew I was going to die. I thought of my sad life; no family, no real friends, my shitty job inputting data at an office job. I closed my eyes and braced for the worst. It felt like ages, but in reality it was likely only a few seconds. I opened my eyes to find the truck had come to a complete stop a few inches in front of me. I was so stunned, I forgot to breathe. I walked around the truck that I was sure would be the end of me. The man was slouched over in the drivers seat, unconscious, a half empty beer bottle in the cupholder. I walked past the truck and looked around. There were a few people in the parking lot along with me, but none of them were moving. I shouted at a lady exiting the store. No reply. I looked into the sky, and saw a group of birds frozen mid-air. That was when it hit me: I did this. Somehow, I had stopped time. I spent the next six hours exploring the world, and found that everything was frozen absolutely still. A man on the sidewalk was dropping his phone, so I picked it up and placed it back in his pocket. A small child riding his scooter was about to crash into a wall, so I turned his scooter around. I was entirely amazed by what was happening, it all felt so surreal. As I was walking through the store, debating whether or not I should take a Flatscreen TV, time began to return to normal. The truck, I thought. I immediately dropped everything I was holding and ran to my car. I needed to get out of the way before my car got hit. I got in, pulled out of the parking lot, and drove off. I never bothered to check if the truck driver was okay. After that night, life became so much easier. I learned how to control my power, and was able to use it to rob a bank, steal any item I desired, get a new car, and break into buildings and houses where I did not belong. It was all very juvenile, but my life had been so boring before. This was the most fun I have had in 15 years. Then, one day, it all caught up to me. It was the one year anniversary of the day I had discovered my ability. I turned on the news on my fancy TV, where a reporter stood in the very parking lot in which I had almost been killed. I turned up the volume. "The holidays can be a rough time for a lot of people. Last year, on this very day, a local veteran drove his truck straight into this pole in what was believed to be a suicide attempt. A local charity aims to raise funds to help people like Eric Stone, to prevent tragic incidents such as this one." I sat in stunned silence. They were talking about the man who almost killed me! But it couldn't have been a suicide attempt. He was driving drunk. I remembered the beer bottle in the cupholder of his car. That night, I went out to test a theory that I hoped to god was wrong. I walked into the local convenience store, scanning the shop. The only other person there was a sad-looking employee, drooped over texting. I concentrated on the subtle movements in the room; the air currents, the sound of thumbs tapping on a phone, a slight creak in the ceiling, and silenced them. When I opened my eyes time was frozen. I used up my time wandering the city looking for trouble that I could stop. I saw a mugging taking place, and stole the knives from the perpetrators. I moved their victim far away, and handcuffed the muggers to a pole in front of the police station. I helped a waitress in a restaurant who had accidentally tipped her trays of food. Soon enough, the movements began to return, slowly but surely. There was a slight breeze. A bird flapped its wings in super-slow motion. I sprinted back to the convenience store, but I was too late. A car drove past me down the road at a normal speed. I rounded the corner, and ran into the store. Just as I arrived, I heard a creaking in the ceiling, the same one I had heard as I was stopping time. Before I could do anything, the ceiling collapsed over the head of the employee. He didn't even have time to look up from his phone before his head was crushed. Oh god Oh god Oh god, I screamed in my head as I backed away from the scene. I killed him. It's my fault that he's dead. I turned and ran. I didn't even get as far as my neighborhood before a black SUV pulled up next to me on the quiet road. Two large men grabbed me by my arms, and jabbed my neck with a needle. I felt drowsy, and before I could react, I fell asleep. I awoke in a small room with concrete walls, my wrists cuffed tightly to a metal table. Across from me sat a large man wearing a generals uniform. He looked at me with cold, piercing eyes. "Don't even think about trying to stop time." I gave an incredulous look. "I don't know what you're talking about." The General didn't flinch. "We have you cuffed to the table tighter than anyone could escape, and even if you did, the only way out of this room is if someone on the outside allows it. Even if you did stop time, you can't escape here." "I didn't mean to." I muttered, frightened. What did they want from me? Were they here to punish me for killing those people? "What didn't you mean to do?" The General gave me an icy stare. "Kill those people." He seemed to hesitate at this, as though I was saying something unexpected. "We do not care about anyone you may have killed. We want you for a different reason." I thought for a moment. They knew I could freeze time. They kidnapped me in a black SUV. The man in front of me was a General, or at least pretending to be. "You work for the government. You want me to stop time for you." He smiled joylessly. "There you go. We want to use your talents to keep this country safe. Are you going to help us, or do we have to force you?" He pulled out a combat knife, and set it on the table. In that moment, I knew what I had to do. I closed my eyes, and felt the presence of the General in front of me. I heard his breath, felt his heat, smelled his odor. I snuffed it all out, and opened my eyes. He sat motionless before me. I tried the cuffs; he was right, there was no way I was getting out of these. But that was not the plan. I reached for the knife. When I was unable to grasp it, I rotated my body in my chair, and used my leg to move it towards me. I sat back down, now holding the knife in both hands, point up. I knew what I had to do. My power only lasted for a few hours. In order for the government to use me as a weapon, I would have to freeze time over and over and over again, killing thousands of people in the process. That wasn't a burden I could live with. I positioned my head above the blade, so as to allow it the path of least resistance up through my eye and into my brain. In a few hours, the General would find a dead man sitting across from him. He would probably have to buy a new table. I bought my head down.

article: Most of the existing denoising algorithms are developed for grayscale images. It is not trivial to extend them for color image denoising since the noise statistics in R, G, and B channels can be very different for real noisy images. In this paper, we propose a multi-channel (MC) optimization model for real color image denoising under the weighted nuclear norm minimization (WNNM) framework. We concatenate the RGB patches to make use of the channel redundancy, and introduce a weight matrix to balance the data fidelity of the three channels in consideration of their different noise statistics. The proposed MC-WNNM model does not have an analytical solution. We reformulate it into a linear equality-constrained problem and solve it via alternating direction method of multipliers. Each alternative updating step has a closed-form solution and the convergence can be guaranteed. Experiments on both synthetic and real noisy image datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed MC-WNNM over state-of-the-art denoising methods.

article: A diverse variety of processes - including recurrent disease episodes, neuron firing, and communication patterns among humans - can be described using inter-event time (IET) distributions. Many such processes are ongoing, although event sequences are only available during a finite observation window. Because the observation time window is more likely to begin or end during long IETs than during short ones, the analysis of such data is susceptible to a bias induced by the finite observation period. In this paper, we illustrate how this length bias is born and how it can be corrected without assuming any particular shape for the IET distribution. To do this, we model event sequences using stationary renewal processes, and we formulate simple heuristics for determining the severity of the bias. To illustrate our results, we focus on the example of empirical communication networks, which are temporal networks that are constructed from communication events. The IET distributions of such systems guide efforts to build models of human behavior, and the variance of IETs is very important for estimating the spreading rate of information in networks of temporal interactions. We analyze several well-known data sets from the literature, and we find that the resulting bias can lead to systematic underestimates of the variance in the IET distributions and that correcting for the bias can lead to qualitatively different results for the tails of the IET distributions.

article: Part I: A week ago, Galaxy 8's Interstellar Detective Bureau dispatched an investigator to mining vessel Tau-9-9 to inquire into details involving the mass murder and data breach on Watcher station Alpha-0-1-1. Security footage was sparse, but it revealed a human astronaut absconding from the station with a small data stick. Security footage at port 119B revealed a security seal from astronauts on Tau-9-9 was used to gain access to the station shortly before the massacre. This station was manned by only two officers. One, a top-decorated pilot in the U.S. Air Force and mother of two named Amanda Bailey. The other, a Harvard-educated mathematician from Japan who played video games as a hobby and spoke 19 different languages named Ken Ichimitzu. The investigator's entrance into the mining ship was unnoticed and silent. The ship appeared unoccupied. It looked ransacked, though. Furniture was torn and clawed through, almost as if by an animal. A small veneer of dust had settled over all, and motion-detecting lights creaked on as he walked down hallways, almost as if they'd been dormant for some time. With the mainframe hard-drive missing, the investigator made his way down several corridors to the captain's quarters. There, he ignited the computer, unfurled a small piece of crinkled paper containing a username and passcode, and accessed the Captain's log file. Captain's Log: 82616 3:30 a.m. Eyes hurt from digging knuckles of my hands into my eyes, trying to wipe away the sleep. I feel trapped. Helpless. Out here on this space station, my computer monitor is really the only area of activity, of newness, of anything echoing life back home. Looks like that buffoon Trump is going to lose. Not much better to beat him, but hey, whoever gets me back home safe and sound, right? I should be catching sheep by now, but something's keeping me awake. I don't feel right about Amanda. My toes won't rest in their shoes, my shoulders feel tight, I'm breathing shallowly, and there's a nameless thickness set into his throat that won't go away. I swear I've looked at the clock ten times in the last minute. It's 3:16 now. Damn it. It had started last week. Astronaut 11A (aka Amanda), had returned on Saturday from her monthly meeting on exoplanet Rebinium with the other watchers on star system Tau-9-9. I had asked her how the meeting went, and curiously she didn't talk much about it. She loves these things, the ideas they have for new exploration and resource management, and all the new people she meets there. But this time she just yawned, and then asked where the bathroom was. It's a small spacecraft. And she's been here for almost a year now. I glanced at her in incredulity, you know, the way you do when you are trying to persuade someone into stopping joking around, to see if they're serious, with that hint of hope and terror that what if she really doesn't know..... my eye brows raised and forehead scrunched in confusion. She immediately sensed my nerves and the gaffe, and laughed, but it was a laugh that was hollow and perfunctory, a laugh like when you are trying to disarm someone, not when you find something funny. Certainly not the kind of giddy laugh I've grown to love about Amanda. But when she turned around to walk away, she took a right turn instead of a left one, and even though I'd turned around out of politeness, so as to hide the fact I was worried, I could hear soft footsteps trying to conceal their way behind my back, retracing steps back to the bathroom. Maybe I'm paranoid. Maybe she just took some strange medicine or something, and was a little delirious. Hence, the fatigue. Who knows. Over and out. Captain's Log: 82716 12:21 a.m. "I don't feel right," were her first words when I saw her the following morning. I asked if she didn't sleep well, and she said it wasn't that. Something in her head, she said, striking her skull sort of violently with the heel of her hand. But she wouldn't talk anymore about it the more I asked. It's not like her. She's one of the most open people I know, a great American in that true Karl Popper sense. I'm worried about her. The work on the ship is going smoothly. She's still crunching out her reports on status of the ununpentium-289 mining operation. This element is extremely friable, with a half life of one-fifth of a second, about as long as it takes you to sneeze. But a couple of important articles are missing, and I can't seem to turn them up anywhere. One of the astronaut suits is gone, and the picture of my wife and kids I keep paper-clipped to my bathroom mirror has disappeared. I can't figure out which is more important. Captain's Log: 82816 Amanda has a massive bruise on the right side of her head. I asked her if she was hitting herself, and she replied in a cloying voice that she was perfectly fine and happy to be awake and at work. I found it dodgy, but I was glad she was okay. Ever since that trip through the teleporter, she's been acting weird. She doesn't eat eggs anymore for breakfast. That was her favorite food. Now it's granola. I also ran a bot program to monitor her computer activities during breakout session from the helm. She's been ignoring attempts by her family to Skype with her lately, which is quite unlike her. When she was in the shower, I snuck into her room to peek around a bit, see if everything was all right. What's unusual is that her own picture of her family, framed on her bureau, it's gone, too. And I still can't find that damned astronaut suit. Captain's Log: 82916 Today we had food delivery. It went well, partly because I did all the work, but partly because Amanda was not around for me to stress about. It was nice just to be by myself, even if the docking, receiving, depressurization, importing, documentation, transportation, and storage and sealing of the materials was a lot of work. It was worth it, to be alone. I never thought I'd want to be alone, that I'd ever write that, out here on this spaceship. But I like it. When Amanda didn't show up for lunch, I knew something was off. Regardless of my personal preference not to see if she was okay, I took a brisk stroll down to dormitories and rapped on her door. After brushing me off with a few grunts, she opened the door. She was naked, dripping with water. Her eyes, they were hungry. She pulled me into her room, threw her thighs around me, and we had sex then and there. She has a husband for God's sake. I felt strange about it, still do. She didn't seem to care about any of it. And when I finished, she rolled away and said she had some work to do on the computer. She didn't even wipe it out, it was trickling out of her onto the chair she was sitting in, beading down like saliva onto the rubber floor. Who is this person? Captain's Log: 83016 There is something disturbing about Amanda. Lest you begin to think this log is becoming a softcore porno, let me officially document that I wanted and didn't want to see her again. Against my better judgment, I scheduled a trace program to generate data about her internet traffic, what she was reading and writing, and in general why she wasn't working from her office desk in the star bay. Shortly after initiating the program, one of the sensors in the docking bay went dark. Putting down the report I was finishing on the station's Silent Running greenhouse garden, I threw on a track suit and jogged across the station to examine the cause for its failure. As I was inspecting the sensor, I sensed someone right behind me, the hairs on the back of my neck stood up. I turned halfway, and out of the corner of my eye a massive figure towered over me. Immediately I threw my back against the wall and cowered, gasping, seconds later realizing it was just Amanda. I yelled at her for sneaking up on me. Her hair was all tangled, knotty, and there was a musky smell pouring out around her, a smell that wasn't attractive. She asked my why I was spying on her. This was when I felt nauseated. She didn't ask it in the sense that she was innocent. It was malicious. There was something malevolent in her voice I had never heard before. But her face was cool, hands flat at her sides, voice monotone, but there was an indistinct contempt running in the background. I bought some time and told her that Tau-9-9 protocol requires documentation of company time during periods of employment, and that I was simply trying to account for her employment hours so that she could get paid - not that I was reading what she was up to. She asked if I had seen the report. I told her I hadn't, which was true. The report was scheduled to finish two hours ago, and I'd just been involved with other things. Immediately she relaxed, and half-smiled. Then she reached past me into the sensor, pulled a wire and linked it to a node, and the room lit up like a police roof light. Before she left, I asked her if she had seen my family photo. There was a kind of dim shaking in her irises. Like something deep in her was stirring from slumber. Then she shook her head, smacked it again hard, turned around and walked out. Just before she left, she said families make one weak, and are inappropriate for this profession. Then the airlock door hissed, and she was gone. Captain's Log: 9116 The report is gone! I logged into my account, plugged into Tau-9-9's mainframe, and tried to access the data file, but it was corrupted. Something in the code had warped, and it was unusable. Things just get weirder and weirder around here. Today Amanda was walking on her hands up and down the star bay, almost singing.

article: We address the problem of unsupervised geometric image-to-image translation. Rather than transferring the style of an image as a whole, our goal is to translate the geometry of an object as depicted in different domains while preserving its appearance characteristics. Our model is trained in an unsupervised fashion, i.e. without the need of paired images during training. article: Knowledge graphs capture entities and relations from long documents and can facilitate reasoning in many downstream applications. These techniques rely on language models and ontologies to understand the meaning of the text and identify entities and their relationships. Machine learning techniques can also be used to extract knowledge graphs, including supervised and unsupervised learning methods. Supervised learning techniques rely on labeled datasets to train models to identify entities and relations, while unsupervised learning techniques can learn patterns and relationships in data without prior labeling. Graph mining techniques can be applied to extract structural patterns from data and identify entities and relations based on their connectivity in a graph. These techniques can be combined with machine learning and natural language processing techniques for more accurate and comprehensive knowledge graph extraction. Overall, selecting the appropriate techniques and approaches for knowledge graph extraction will depend on the specific use case and data available.

article: I had lived through the most stereotypical uni experience. I met her at the fresher's party. We got drunk. Danced. Snogged. And ended the night in her flat. As I sat, putting several bags full of purchases I would never use around my seat. I looked at her ordering the coffee and noticed for the first time just how stressed she was looking. She was gently rubbing her temple. That wasn't a good sign. That always meant she was thinking about something she wasn't entirely comfortable with. She came back with her drink and had ordered me a caramel macchiato. That wasn't right. I only drank Americanos or espressos. She sat down, not looking at me for a while. Just staring at the coffee lid and breathing. I finally gave in " what is it? why are you acting weird? " she looked at me blankly. She cleared her throat and said " I'm going to be direct. I've been seeing someone else for the past three years. I'm in love with him. He's met our kids. And I'm thinking...no, I'm going to be " she stopped as a single tear ran down her cheek. I felt like I'd been hit on the chest with a baseball bat. I felt winded. I felt a tightness in my chest and arm. I struggled to say anything. She went on " the kids are with him right now. I'm sorry. I'm...I'm leaving you. I'm sorry " I felt the tears stinging my eyes. I said the only thing I could " why? " she was wiping tears from her eyes now. She gave a sarcastic laugh. " Why? Why do you think? You haven't even noticed that I've been falling out of love with you for the past five years. After we had Gillian, I've just not been able to connect with you. I had to take a break from work, while all you did was work. When are you ever home Jack? When are you ever present in the moment. I met him. I started falling for him. I love him and I realised I haven't felt this love with you, ever ." I felt rage. I felt sorrow. I felt pity. I felt betrayal. It all started going dark. I felt myself slipping from my seat. My chest tightening so much, I couldn't get air in. My lungs burned and my arms felt heavy as lead. I fell to the floor but didn't feel it. I was just aware my view had changed. I was now looking at the lights on the ceiling. I was literally heartbroken. I could barely move my lips. But I was determined to get these words out. I coughed, more than whispered " never again...I will love...never again ." I didn't know where I was. I felt I was in a dreamlike state. I felt like I was walking on clouds. When I looked down. I realised, I actually was walking on clouds. I didn't know where I was walking towards. But just that I needed to walk forward and up those steps made out of clouds. I was looking around me in wonder. This was truly amazing, but where was I. Was I dead? I felt at peace, so maybe I was. I felt a light shining. It was so bright I had to put my hand up so I could still walk without tripping. Then I saw a shape bathed in the light. As I got closer, the shape started to become familiar. It was a woman. With long golden blonde, or wait was it auburn? No, I think she was a brunette. Every ray of light gave her hair a different colour. The closer I got, the larger she became. Until I was standing at the foot of a ten-foot-tall woman. She was wearing a robe with a gold coloured rope as a belt. Or was it a rope made of gold. She looked at me and smiled. I could try describing her beauty, but that would be an offense to just how beautiful she looked. She said " I hear a lot of people say they'll never love again, but only ever so often does someone mean it from their heart.
